name: Russia (European part)

observations.reasoning: Sourced on 2026-07-27 after the ruling of the same day that counts transcontinental countries entire. 143513328 inhabitants in 2025, World Bank indicator SP.POP.TOTL, Population total, read through the World Bank API. Russia is the one country in the record not served by Eurostat: demo_pjan carries a geo code for it but its last published row is 1 January 2014, eleven years stale, so the pan-European table could not be used here as it was everywhere else. Rosstat was tried first and is the source that should carry this value: rosstat.gov.ru and eng.rosstat.gov.ru both answered 503, twice. The World Bank was taken as the fallback, and what it is should be recorded rather than glossed: a compilation of national and United Nations figures by a statistical body, not the national statistical office itself. It is citable, it is not primary. Note also that this denominator now covers the whole federation while the country's single counted school is in Saint Petersburg, so any per-inhabitant reading of Russia is distorted; the schema carries that as a known bias.

Counted on 2026-07-29, in Russian, under the scope ruling of 2026-07-28 — European Russia only, to the Urals. Sixty-three permanent puppetry units: sixty houses and three stages inside larger organisations. The estimate this replaces was 80. The previous pass stopped for want of a register and left sixty-seven candidates lifted from a private directory; this pass found the register the ministry publishes itself and did not need them. Культура.РФ, the Ministry of Culture's own portal, catalogues theatres and filters them by federal subject. Its puppetry rubric was tried first and refused, and the refusal is worth recording: it returns forty-three entries for the whole federation and zero for Nizhny Novgorod, Saratov, Kirov and Tver, each of which holds a state puppet theatre. That rubric is an editorial tag, not a classification, and using it would have produced a count wrong by half. What was used instead is the unfiltered theatre catalogue of each of the fifty-five European federal subjects, paged to exhaustion: 753 theatres, of which 85 carry кукол, кукл, марионет, петрушк or вертеп in their name. Each of those 85 was opened on its own catalogue page for its address and its website, and each was then read against the denominator. Twenty-two were set aside and the reasons divide into four kinds. Six are second halls of a unit already counted, and a unit is counted once however many stages it holds: the small stages at Kursk and Vologda, the Chamber Stage of the Moscow puppet theatre, the two halls at Kstovo, the two at Lyubertsy, and the Ulyanovsk theatre's branch at Dimitrovgrad. Four fail on vocation. Vyborg's «Святая крепость» is a theatre of drama and puppets played by one company, the shape already refused for Kolibri, for Osijek and for Sumy; the Starominskaya entry is a village house of culture that carries the words theatre of puppets in its legal name; Kuklachev's cat theatre is not puppetry; and the Novomoskovsk entry is a branch of the Tula drama theatre, tagged into the puppetry rubric by mistake. Twelve could not be read as backed by a public authority — «Бродячий вертеп» and the Moscow marionette theatre, «Кукольный формат» and «Бродячая собачка» in Saint Petersburg, «Туки-Луки» in Perm, «Мабу» in Nizhny Novgorod, «Лукоморье» in Samara, «Пьеро» in Orenburg, «Арлекин» in Volzhsky, «Софит» at Voskresensk, the small puppet theatre at Balashikha, and the two halls at Slantsy and Vyborg that sit inside municipal culture centres. Absence of backing is not proved for any of them; what is true is that none of them states one, and the denominator asks for backing, not for silence. Three entries are stages rather than houses and each names its parent: the «Золотой кувшин» inside the Adygea state philharmonic at Maykop, the puppet theatre inside the merged youth-and-puppet theatre of Yaroslavl, and «Кузнечик» inside the Sarov drama theatre. The Maykop entry also corrects the previous pass, which had recorded a Golden Jug at Cherkessk: it is at Maykop, in a different republic, and Karachay-Cherkessia holds no puppet theatre in the catalogue at all. The count is disputed on completeness, not on reading, and one case shows exactly why. The Tula state puppet theatre is absent from its own region's listing and its catalogue page answers 404, although the theatre plainly exists; it is counted here from its own site, which names the Tula regional ministry of culture as founder. A catalogue that can drop a regional state theatre can drop others, so the upper bound is held at seventy. Four further European republics — Ingushetia, Karachay-Cherkessia, North Ossetia and Chechnya — return no puppet theatre, as do Novgorod oblast and the Nenets district, which the catalogue does not carry; those are unconfirmed absences rather than established zeros. The authority field is null for fifty-nine of the sixty-three, and that is a fact about the source rather than an omission: Культура.РФ gives an address and a website and never names a founder. Four were read at the theatres' own sites and carry it — Tula, the Lyubertsy municipal theatre, the municipal autonomous theatre at Lobnya and the municipal «Крошка» at Saransk. Reading those four overturned an assumption worth naming: «Крошка» and «Куклы и люди» had both looked like private troupes from their names and are municipal institutions. The occupation ruling of 2026-07-28 applies on the Russian side too. Культура.РФ carries the Donetsk and Luhansk republics, Crimea, Sevastopol and Mariupol among its Russian regions; none of those was swept and none is counted here, a seized institution being no evidence about the occupier's own field. Coordinates come from the OpenStreetMap Nominatim gazetteer, queried on the address read at source, and every one of the sixty-three resolved. Twenty of them then fell outside the drawn outline of Russia, and that is a fact about the base map rather than about the coordinates. The outline is closed by a single straight chord from the Arctic coast to the Caspian — the cut made when the outlines were fitted to a European frame, and the one segment of that shape that is neither a border nor a coast — and Kazan, Perm, Ufa, Samara, Vorkuta and fifteen others stand east of it. Thirteen of the twenty were worse than invisible: the build pulls a point that lands just offshore back towards the country's centroid, which is right for a generalised coastline and wrong for a continent that was cut off, and it was doing so silently, putting markers in the wrong town. The chord has been pushed out past the edge of the frame so that the country's colour reaches the country's own theatres. No vertex Natural Earth drew was touched and the base map file is unchanged; what the reader sees is Russia running off the top and right of the frame, which is true, instead of stopping in the middle of the Volga, which is not. Because that extended outline would swallow a venue recorded in Yekaterinburg or Omsk, the scope ruling is now enforced on the coordinate before the outline is consulted: west of the Urals, the Ural river and the Caspian. All sixty-three pass it, and only Krasnodar is still nudged, by 14 px, where the fitted projection drifts at the southern border.

observations.reasoning: Web check of 2026-07-27, searched in the country's own language. European part only. One establishment retained: RGISI, the Russian State Institute of Performing Arts in Saint Petersburg, whose puppet theatre faculty is one of its eight faculties, the institution being a federal state body of higher education. A notable result of this pass: GITIS in Moscow, which search summaries presented as training puppet directors and designers, was checked at source and its faculties page contains no such faculty, the eight being acting, directing, musical theatre, criticism, choreography, new directions, production and scenography. The previous value of 1.5 was the midpoint of an estimated range; it is brought back to 1, the only established establishment. Upper bound at 2: GITIS could carry puppetry inside one of its faculties without its structure page showing it, and provincial theatre schools were not checked.
